links.targetTitle: Keel cannot raise its own rate limits: writing them is admin

title: Only admin can set a rate limit's envelope; Controllers may only spend and restore inside it
content:
The rate-limit contract splits its interface by role. `setRateLimitData(key, maxAmount, slope, ...)` is `onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE)` (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.2.1.3.2), while `triggerRateLimitDecrease` and `triggerRateLimitIncrease` are `onlyRole(CONTROLLER)` (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.2.1.3.4 and .3.5).

The distinction is between the *envelope* and the *position inside it*. Admin — Sky Governance via the Spark Proxy — decides how much capacity exists and how fast it regenerates. The Controllers, driven by the Relayer, can only consume capacity and give it back. No operational actor can widen its own limit.

Both trigger functions also begin with `require(maxAmount > 0, "RateLimits/zero-maxAmount")`. A limit whose `maxAmount` is zero does not merely have no capacity — every attempt to use it reverts. Zero is therefore the disable switch for an operation, and it is a switch only admin can flip.

That matters for reading the parameter tables correctly. `LIMIT_USDS_BURN` at zero does not mean burning is throttled to nothing; it means the key is dead, which is consistent with burning being accounted as a credit to the mint key instead. More generally, the pair (maxAmount = 0 to disable, admin-only to change) gives governance a per-operation kill switch that is finer-grained than the Freezer's global halt and slower to exercise — the right combination for permanently retiring a capability rather than pausing the system.
description: setRateLimitData is DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE while triggerRateLimitDecrease/Increase are CONTROLLER-only, and both revert on a zero maxAmount — making zero the switch that disables an operation.
